newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lawyers work to free thousands of boatpeople in HK.
newsitem.headline: Lawyers work to free thousands of boatpeople in HK.

text.p: Thousands of Vietnamese boatpeople could be freed from detention camps by the end of the year if they succeed in what would be the biggest habeas corpus action ever in the British colony, their lawyer said on Friday.

Lawyer Pam Baker of the advocacy group Refugee Concern is leading the fight to secure the release of up to 4,000 boatpeople, most of them women and children, who have spent as much as eight years behind barbed wire.
"What we are saying is, the time that has elapsed is unreasonable. (If) you can't remove them, you have got to let them out," Baker said by telephone.
Most lack the papers or other proof to show they are Vietnamese, and Hanoi has declined to give assurances they would be accepted back into the country if deported from Hong Kong.
Around 12,000 boatpeople languish in Hong Kong detention camps, the end of a human tidal wave to flee Vietnam in the aftermath of a war that ended over 20 years ago.
Some 7,000 have been cleared for return by the Vietnamese government and await repatriation, said Mak Kwok-wah, a spokesman for the Hong Kong government's security branch.
More than 260 boatpeople succeeded in securing their freedom earlier this year on the grounds Vietnam would not accept them back.
The British colony's highest appeal court, the Privy Council, ruled they were illegally detained and ordered their immediate release.
Mak said Hong Kong was holding talks with Vietnam in a bid to persuade the authorities there to take back the 4,000 and speed up the entire repatriation process.
Hong Kong aims to clear its camps before the middle of next year when the British colony reverts to China.
